title: Functions, graphs and transformations
summary: Equations of lines, domain and range, composite and inverse functions, and how translations, stretches and reflections change a graph.

keyterms.definition: Steepness of a line: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁); parallel lines have equal gradients.
Lines are perpendicular when m₁ × m₂ = −1, so each gradient is the negative reciprocal of the other.
The set of input values for which a function is defined.
The set of output values a function takes over its domain.
(f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)): apply g first, then f.
f⁻¹ reverses f, so f(f⁻¹(x)) = x; its graph is the reflection of f in y = x.
A function where each output comes from exactly one input; only these have inverses.
A shift of a graph: y = f(x − h) + k moves it h right and k up.
y = pf(x) stretches vertically by factor p; y = f(qx) stretches horizontally by factor 1/q.
y = −f(x) reflects in the x-axis; y = f(−x) reflects in the y-axis.

questions.prompt: Find the gradient of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 11).
What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to y = 2x − 5?
questions.explanation: Take the negative reciprocal of 2.

questions.text: The domain of f(x) = √(x − 3) is x ___ 3.
questions.explanation: The expression under the square root must be non-negative, and x = 3 gives √0 = 0.

questions.statement: For f(x) = x², x ∈ ℝ, the range is f(x) ≥ 0.
questions.explanation: A square is never negative and every non-negative value is reached.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x². Find (f ∘ g)(3).
questions.explanation: g(3) = 9 first, then f(9) = 19. 49 is (g ∘ f)(3): the order matters.
Swap x and y: x = (y − 4)/3, so y = 3x + 4. Undo the operations in reverse order.

questions.text: The graph of y = f⁻¹(x) is the reflection of y = f(x) in the line y = ___.
questions.explanation: Swapping x and y reflects every point (a, b) to (b, a).

questions.statement: f(x) = x², x ∈ ℝ, has an inverse function.
questions.explanation: It is not one-to-one (f(2) = f(−2)). Restricting the domain to x ≥ 0 gives the inverse √x.

questions.prompt: Match each line to its description.
questions.explanation: Rearrange to y = mx + c to read off the gradient and intercept.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to find the inverse of f(x) = 2x + 5.
questions.explanation: Swap, then make y the subject.

questions.prompt: y = f(x − 2) + 3 is the graph of y = f(x) translated by…
questions.explanation: Inside the bracket the shift is opposite to the sign: x − 2 moves right.

options: a vertical stretch, scale factor ⅓
a horizontal stretch, scale factor ⅓
questions.explanation: Multiplying the output by 3 triples every y-coordinate.

questions.text: y = f(2x) is a horizontal stretch with scale factor ___.
questions.explanation: Each x-coordinate is halved, because the same output is reached at half the input.

questions.statement: y = −f(x) is the reflection of y = f(x) in the x-axis.
questions.explanation: Every y-coordinate changes sign.

questions.prompt: The point (4, −1) lies on y = f(x). Which point lies on y = f(−x)?
questions.explanation: Reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of x only.

questions.prompt: y = x² is transformed to y = (x + 1)² − 5. Where is the vertex?
questions.explanation: Translate (0, 0) one unit left and five units down.

questions.text: Stretch y = x² vertically by factor 2, then translate it 3 units up: y = 2x² + ___.
questions.explanation: The stretch gives 2x²; the translation then adds 3. Doing them in the other order gives 2x² + 6.

questions.statement: y = f(x) + 4 and y = f(x + 4) are the same transformation.
questions.explanation: f(x) + 4 moves the graph up 4; f(x + 4) moves it left 4.

questions.prompt: Match each transformation to its effect.
questions.explanation: Changes outside f act on y as expected; changes inside act on x in reverse.

questions.prompt: Track the point (1, 1) on y = x² as it is mapped to y = 2(x − 3)² + 1.
questions.explanation: Check: 2(4 − 3)² + 1 = 3, so (4, 3) is on the final curve.
